title: Silicon Catalyst 2026 Semiconductor Industry Forum – What’s Next for AI, Quantum, and Space
gist: Recap of the ninth Silicon Catalyst Semiconductor Industry Forum: GlobalFoundries CEO Tim Breen argued AI data-center bottlenecks are shifting from compute to memory, power delivery and optical connectivity, while a panel (Mayfield's Navin Chaddha, Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park's Harley Johnson, Anderon's Dan Dechene) forecast 'Work as a Service', a renewed premium on manufacturing, fault-tolerant quantum around 2028–2029, and a fabless-foundry model for quantum.

insights.claim: GlobalFoundries CEO Tim Breen argues that as AI data centers move toward gigawatt-scale power and megawatt-scale racks, bottlenecks are shifting beyond computation into memory, power delivery and connectivity.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Look past GPUs to memory, power-delivery and interconnect suppliers as the next AI-capex beneficiaries.
insights.locator: As data centers expand toward gigawatt-scale

insights.claim: Breen says AI data-center energy efficiency increasingly depends on picojoules-per-bit metrics, advanced power delivery needs unprecedented current densities, and silicon photonics/optical communication is becoming essential to move data.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Optical interconnect and power-management silicon are structural growth vectors in AI infrastructure.

insights.claim: GlobalFoundries, which has invested in silicon photonics for more than a decade, views the rapid emergence of optical connectivity as validation of its technology strategy.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: GlobalFoundries is positioning as an AI-optics beneficiary rather than a leading-edge node player; watch photonics revenue disclosure.
insights.locator: For GlobalFoundries, which has invested in silicon photonics

insights.claim: Breen expects future semiconductor innovation to rely increasingly on specialized materials, heterogeneous integration, power management, sensing, connectivity and application-specific architectures, not just advanced process nodes.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Supports specialty-foundry and advanced-packaging exposure alongside leading-edge logic.

insights.claim: Breen frames semiconductors as having moved from behind the scenes to the center of the global economy, with AI data-center expansion among the largest infrastructure investments in modern history and manufacturing becoming increasingly strategic.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Supports a strategic/geopolitical premium on manufacturing capacity.
insights.locator: He explained that for decades, semiconductors operated

insights.claim: Mayfield's Navin Chaddha predicts the next technology transition moves from Software as a Service to 'Work as a Service' (WaaS), where organizations buy completed work from AI digital workers and physical robots instead of software tools.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: SaaS seat-based pricing faces disruption; outcome-priced AI service companies may capture value.
insights.locator: From Software as a Service to Work as a Service

insights.claim: Chaddha estimates about $30 trillion is spent annually on digital labor and $30 trillion on physical labor; if AI captures 20%, it creates a $12 trillion market opportunity.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: A TAM framing for AI agents and robotics that VCs are underwriting against.

insights.claim: Under WaaS, software platforms, AI models and semiconductors become essential infrastructure for thousands of AI-service companies, and leaders compete on the economic value of work performed rather than software products sold.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Infrastructure layers retain value while application-layer competition shifts to outcomes.

insights.claim: Breen argues the semiconductor economic model is changing from cost reduction toward value for the work AI computing enables, making manufacturing capabilities, advanced materials and specialized technologies more valuable and hard to replicate quickly.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Supports pricing power and multiple re-rating for foundries and materials suppliers.
insights.locator: Hardware Moves Back to the Center of Value Creation

insights.claim: Harley Johnson notes AI can dramatically accelerate materials discovery, but converting discoveries into manufacturable products remains extraordinarily difficult; the panel concluded manufacturing expertise stays a key differentiator.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: AI-for-science gains bottleneck at fabrication; manufacturing know-how is the scarce asset.
insights.quote: AI may accelerate invention, but manufacturing expertise will remain a critical source of competitive differentiation

insights.claim: Anderon's Dechene described quantum computing as at the 'beginning of the beginning', and both he and Harley Johnson point to 2028–2029 as a potentially important period for fault-tolerant quantum computing advances.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Dates a potential catalyst window for quantum equities; near-term revenue claims should be discounted.

insights.claim: Johnson cautioned that quantum computing's 'ChatGPT moment' may not be a single event, with commercial momentum instead building through demonstrations of compelling applications.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Expect gradual quantum adoption, not a step-change re-rating.

insights.claim: Chaddha argues quantum computing needs credible, economically valuable use cases rather than a revolutionary consumer application, and startups should target narrow markets, gain traction and expand.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Screen quantum startups for niche commercial traction over grand platform claims.

insights.claim: Anderon is described as a quantum technology company spun out of IBM, with Dan Dechene heading its foundry business.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: A new IBM-linked quantum foundry player worth tracking.

insights.claim: The panel argued quantum companies should leverage existing semiconductor wafer fab, test, packaging and integration infrastructure rather than duplicate it, so quantum could adopt a fabless-foundry model much earlier than conventional semiconductors did.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Foundries with quantum-capable processes (e.g. GlobalFoundries) could become picks-and-shovels for quantum.
insights.quote: The emerging quantum industry could therefore adopt a fabless-foundry model much earlier in its development than conventional semiconductors did.
insights.locator: The Semiconductor Foundry Model Could Accelerate Quantum

insights.claim: Testing superconducting qubits can require cryogenic environments and lengthy measurement procedures, a distinct scaling challenge for quantum manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Cryogenic test capacity is a potential bottleneck and niche opportunity in quantum supply chains.

insights.claim: Chaddha observed venture capital is heavily concentrated in AI, potentially starving quantum and other emerging technologies, and warned about extraordinarily high private valuations unsupported by business performance.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Signals VC-level concern about AI private-market froth; non-AI deep tech may be under-funded relative to opportunity.

insights.claim: Panelists pointed to public investment, shared infrastructure and government-supported benchmarking programs as key to accelerating quantum commercialization alongside VCs, universities and manufacturers.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Government funding programs are a leading indicator for quantum ecosystem formation.

insights.claim: Chaddha spontaneously proposed a quantum-focused addition to Silicon Catalyst, offering Mayfield's participation to jump-start an initiative for quantum startups.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Early sign of VC appetite for structured quantum incubation.
insights.locator: The panel also ended with a spontaneous proposal
